panel.summary: SOUND. The round-12 delta resolves the round-11 false-deny regressions without opening accidental false grants: restricting the unknowable trigger to aliasing programs frees `git diff "${BASE:-main}" HEAD` and `echo "${A:-x}" "${B:-y}"`; the destination-only rule keeps `cp "${SRC:-in}" out.txt` then git push free while tracking out.txt; per-item for-loop values fix `for x in a b; do x+=.sh`. Low, non-blocking: operands[-1] assumes a positional destination, so `-t`/`--target-directory` forms are an adversarial edge case.

NOT SOUND. High — unknown symlink sources can produce a new false grant: `ln -s "${SRC:-go.sh}" link; KARTA_SKIP_GATE=1 echo "git commit -m y" > link; bash go.sh`. ln creates link -> go.sh; the redirect writes through the symlink into go.sh; bash go.sh runs the commit without the hatch. The delta treats only the last operand as a possible unknown destination, so go.sh never enters written. Fix: for symlink creation, conservatively set written_anywhere when a triggered ln -s has an unknown source.

SOUND. Low, not blocking: non-aliaser wrappers (`sudo cp`, `xargs cp`, `env -i cp`) lose the unknown-destination arm — a deliberate construction the delta's comment already scopes; only one alias hop is followed (pre-existing); single-operand aliasers newly arm (rare). New triggers are a strict subset of the old for two or more operands; the last operand governs where bytes land; per-item for values are strictly more accurate. No accidental grant, no realistic false deny.

SOUND. Medium, below the blocking bar: _ALIASERS is incomplete — `dd if="${SRC:-go.sh}" of=out.sh; bash out.sh` after a commit-text write is granted; a two-hop alias through an unknowable name, which the docstring scopes out as deliberate. Low: operands[-1] misreads the destination for -t DIR forms; per-item for-loop values can exceed the 64-expansion cap (conservative deny). No everyday false deny.

SOUND. The delta is correct; no false grants and no everyday false denies. Lower severity: _is_aliaser covers only git mv among git subcommands; dd and tar are absent from _ALIASERS, exploitable only through deliberate construction. The for-loop per-item change matches bash; the destination-only check mirrors how the aliasers place the new file.

NOT SOUND. High — false-deny regression: `cp --target-directory=build "${SRC:-README.md}"; KARTA_SKIP_GATE=1 grep -n "git commit" f.py > hits.txt; git push` — _operands drops the option, leaving only the unknowable source as the last operand, so written_anywhere is set and git push is denied. Fix: recognise destination-carrying options before applying the last-operand rule.
